content:
Floats in Lean 4.33 will no longer be opaque, see this post. As discussed in the post, the new float model does not relate floats to reals. A Flocq port would build such a relation and would be a useful complement to the new float model.

I have sketched a starting point of a port. At the moment, it boils down to the proof that a sound rounding strategy produces (generalized) floats, modelled as a subtype of reals.

I am aware of a couple of existing projects on floats:

  1. FloatSpec is a faithful translation of Flocq. My starting point can be viewed as a cleaned up version of a small part of this.
  2. flean2 doesn't seem to be very close to Flocq.
  3. fp-lean is for bitblasting float proofs.
  4. TorchLean contains some parts of Flocq-like floats.

I have been thinking about numerical analysis in Lean and I wasn't quite satisfied with any of these. So I decided to sketch the starting point.
Discussion of this project happens at #general > Discussion for Flocq port
